title: A Glimpse of Glory
verse: And he was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and his clothes became white as light. Then Moses and Elijah also appeared before them, talking with him.
observation: I wonder if it was possible to get used to seeing Jesus every day. They would see amazing things so much that it might have been possible to develop a kind of apathy toward the miraculous. This day probably set everyone straight. Without knowing it was coming, Jesus let the “veil” slip a little and allowed His body to transform into a glorified state. I wonder if this is why Peter was so adamant that he would go with Jesus to the death. After seeing Jesus in a moment of His glory, he could not unsee this majesty. Peter is still talking about it when he tells the story to Mark so that it eventually becomes part of that Gospel. He’s even talking about it years later when he writes what we call 2 Peter. A moment of God’s glory marked him for life. This can be the same for us. A moment of glory can change it all.
application: Spend time in God’s presence and focus on worshiping God. See God for who He is, not just all He has done. He is the King of kings and the Lord of lords. Then, carry that with you throughout the day.
prayer: Thank You, Jesus, our King, for being a glorious King.
